---
title: "3. What TDA extracts"
description: "An intuitive picture of what topological features are, before any algebra."
---

<!-- VIDEO: paste your YouTube link, then delete the comment markers and the /* */ -->
<!-- {{</* video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YOUR_VIDEO_ID */>}} -->

Imagine drawing a ball of radius $r$ around every data point and slowly increasing $r$.

- At small $r$ every point is its own **component**.
- As $r$ grows, balls overlap and components **merge**.
- Sometimes the balls form a ring around an empty region: a **loop** is born.
- Grow $r$ further and the hole fills in: the loop **dies**.

Features that survive for a long range of $r$ are likely to be real structure; short-lived ones are usually noise.
Recording every birth and death gives a *persistence barcode* or *persistence diagram*.
